title: Fidelity vs Cost Sensitivity Simulator: Spec and Lab Guide
author: Evelyn Chen
body:
Overview
--------
This document defines the Fidelity vs Cost Sensitivity Simulator (FCS-Sim), a reproducible synthetic experiment platform and accompanying lab guide used to quantify trade-offs between output fidelity (quality), per-token cost, and latency across model variants, quantization profiles, batching configurations, and routing policies. The simulator is intended to produce actionable guidance for: model-variant selection, quantization rollouts, batching/autoscale configuration, and routing fallback strategies.

Motivation
----------
Teams frequently need to answer questions such as: 
- How much output quality do we lose if we switch from fp16 to 8-bit quantized kernels at 512-token prompts for my "search summarization" workload?
- For a given SLO (p99 <= 250ms), what batching and warmstart settings minimize cost while preserving fidelity?
- Which model variants should be in the warm path vs fallback path to maximize successful responses under capacity-constrained bursts?

The FCS-Sim lets engineers and SREs run controlled, configurable simulations combining: sampled production request traces, adjustable kernel latency and cost models, fidelity regression models (from eval scores on representative prompt sets), and routing policy emulation.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
- In-scope: offline simulation of request streams; cost & latency estimation per token; fidelity (quality) projection using calibrated mappings from eval datasets to production metrics; scenario analysis for rollout decisioning.
- Out-of-scope: online A/B in production, end-user subjective quality scoring (human studies), and per-request semantic acceptability adjudication. Use FCS-Sim outputs to design conservative canaries and human-in-the-loop tests.

Architecture overview
---------------------
The simulator is composed of the following modules (service names used in our infra):

- trace_ingestor (python service): ingests sampled request traces from production telemetry or synthetic generators and normalizes request metadata (model, prompt_length, user_tier, timestamp, route_id).
- kernel_latency_model (go): stores latency distributions and kernel-specific cost-per-token for GPU/CPU variants; supports parametric perturbation (thermal throttling, NVLink degradation).
- fidelity_model_store (json/yaml): mapping of model variant x quantization profile -> expected fidelity deltas for named prompt-sets (e.g., summarization-v1, search-qa-v2) calibrated by eval harness.
- routing_emulator (rust): simulates smart routing policies (latency-first, cost-first, tiered-fallback), replica pools, and capacity constraints.
- batch_simulator (python): implements batching logic (continuous batching, fixed-window batchers) and models warmstart/warmup effects on KV cache and model state.
- aggregator_and_reporter (notebook + CLI): aggregates metrics, produces CSV/HTML reports, and generates experiment artifacts for storage in s3://redwood-fcs-sim/experiments/.

Data flow (high level):
1) trace_ingestor -> normalized request stream
2) routing_emulator + kernel_latency_model + batch_simulator -> per-request latency & cost estimates
3) fidelity_model_store -> per-request fidelity delta (relative to baseline)
4) aggregator_and_reporter -> consolidated scenario metrics and visualizations

Key metrics produced
--------------------
- latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99 (ms) per route and aggregated
- cost_per_1000_tokens (USD) and cost_per_successful_response (USD)
- expected_fidelity_delta (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim delta or custom eval score delta) per prompt-set
- SLA_breach_rate: fraction of requests > SLO threshold (configurable; default 250ms p99)
- perceived_degradation_rate: fraction of requests expected to have fidelity delta > user-provided threshold
- fallback_frequency: percent of requests routed to fallback variants

Experiment protocol (recommended reproducible steps)
---------------------------------------------------
1) Define objective and acceptance criteria. Example: "Allow quantized variant rollout to 20% traffic if perceived_degradation_rate <= 2% and p99 latency <= 280ms."
2) Select input trace: either production-sampled trace (recommended: 24h window, sample 1% uniformly) or synthetic (see "Synthetic generators" below).
3) Choose baseline configuration: baseline_model_variant=redwood-large-fp16; baseline_batching=continuous-8ms; baseline_kv_warm=warm_cache_on
4) Define scenarios: list of configurations to sweep (model variants, quant profiles, batching windows, warmstart fraction, routing policy). Use the scenario YAML schema below.
5) Run simulator: fcs-sim run --config experiments/quant-rollout-2027.yaml --out experiments/results/quant-rollout-2027/
6) Review report: open experiments/results/quant-rollout-2027/summary.html and run fcs-sim analyze --experiment experiments/results/quant-rollout-2027/ --focus "p99,perceived_degradation_rate"
7) Triage and decision: if acceptance criteria are met, produce rollout playbook for canary (see "Rollout playbook" section).

Synthetic generators
--------------------
- prompt_length_sampler: parametric generator producing heavy-tail length distributions matching product area (chat vs embedding vs summarization).
- concurrency_bursts: generator that creates short-duration spikes to stress warmstart and autoscale logic.
- adversarial_prompts: curated prompt set to expose hallucination/regression-sensitive cases (kept in eval-harness repository).

Scenario YAML schema (example)
-----------------------------
Below is a minimal scenario file used to launch a batch of sweeps.

```
name: quant-rollout-2027
trace: s3://redwood-traces/prod-samples/2027-01-01-sampled-1pct.json
baseline:
  model_variant: redwood-large-fp16
  batching:
    mode: continuous
    max_delay_ms: 8
  kv_warm: true
scenarios:
  - name: q8a-small-batch
    model_variant: redwood-large-q8a
    batching:
      mode: fixed_window
      window_ms: 12
    kv_warm: false
  - name: q4_kv_warm
    model_variant: redwood-large-q4
    batching:
      mode: continuous
      max_delay_ms: 6
    kv_warm: true
routing_policies:
  - latency_first
  - cost_first
```

Example CLI
-----------
- Run a single scenario: 
  fcs-sim run --scenario experiments/quant-rollout-2027.yaml --only q8a-small-batch --output-dir /tmp/fcs-output/
- Aggregate results: 
  fcs-sim aggregate --input /tmp/fcs-output/ --format csv --out /tmp/fcs-output/summary.csv

Calibration and fidelity mapping
--------------------------------
Fidelity projections are only as good as the calibrated mapping between offline eval scores and observed production user satisfaction. We maintain a fidelity_model_store entry per model+profile that contains:
- eval_dataset_ids (list of eval harness prompt-set IDs)
- fitted_mapping: JSON containing coefficients for a linear/logistic model that maps eval-score delta -> perceived_degradation_probability
- data_version: git sha of eval harness run used for fit

Example fidelity model store entry (YAML snippet):
```
model: redwood-large-q8a
eval_datasets:
  - summarization-v1
  - search-qa-v2
mapping:
  type: logistic
  intercept: -3.2
  coef_eval_delta: 4.1
  note: calibrated on user-sentiment A/B from 2026-08 study
```

Acceptance criteria examples (templates)
--------------------------------------
- Conservative rollout for core products: perceived_degradation_rate <= 1.5% and p99_latency <= baseline_p99 + 30ms and cost_per_1000_tokens reduction >= 12%
- Experimental rollout for low-risk routes: perceived_degradation_rate <= 5% and SLA_breach_rate <= 0.5%

Report outputs and artifacts
---------------------------
Each experiment run produces:
- summary.html (visual dashboards: latency curves, fidelity vs cost scatterplots, waterfall of fallback routing)
- metrics.csv (per-scenario numeric outputs)
- raw_sim_log.jsonl (per-request simulated decisions and annotations)
- experiment_manifest.yaml (scenario + simulator version + seed)

Interpreting results: common signatures and recommended actions
------------------------------------------------------------
1) Latency decrease but fidelity loss concentrated in short prompts: suggests quantization interacts with decoding temperature; recommended: run focused eval on short-prompt prompt-sets and consider hybrid routing for short prompts to fp16 variants.
2) Cost falls but SLA_breach_rate spikes on bursts: batching/warmstart reduction may be exposing cold-cache latency; recommended: increase warmstart fraction or provide small reserved warm VMs for critical routes.
3) Perceived_degradation concentrated on certain user_tiers: may indicate dataset mismatch — gate rollout behind user_tier filter and run targeted human evaluation.

Rollout playbook (short)
------------------------
1) Canary (1% traffic, 12h): monitor p99 latency, perceived_degradation_rate, fallback_frequency.
2) If perceived_degradation_rate > acceptance -> abort and open RFC with MLOps and product.
3) If metrics stable -> ramp to 5% over 24h, then 20% over 48h, running A/B evaluation with subjective checks at 20%.
4) Full rollout only after 7-day stability window and no regression alerts.

Runbook: when simulator flags an unexpected regression
----------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm input trace and fidelity mapping versions from experiment_manifest.yaml.
2) Re-run experiment with seed fixed and increased sampling to verify non-determinism is not the cause.
3) Run targeted microbenchmarks (see bench-kit) reproducing the specific kernel stack under the same payload.
4) If kernel latency model appears mismatched, escalate to runtime-kernel team (owner: @runtime-kernel) with raw_sim_log.jsonl and a short hypothesis.

Configuration table (operational knobs)
--------------------------------------
| knob                     | type      | default | notes |
|--------------------------|-----------|---------|-------|
| max_delay_ms             | int       | "8"     | Max continuous batching delay |
| batching_mode            | enum      | "continuous" | [continuous,fixed_window] |
| warmstart_fraction       | float     | "0.8"   | Fraction of replicas with warmed KV cache |
| kernel_cost_multiplier   | float     | "1.0"   | Apply to cost model to simulate premium GPUs |
| routing_policy           | enum      | "latency_first" | cost_first, tiered, latency_first |

(Represented here as strings to comply with doc schema.)

Ownership, testing, and CI
--------------------------
- Code owner: eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-team (primary: @evelyn_chen).
- CI: every pull request must run a unit smoke-run on a 1k-request synthetic trace (fcs-sim ci --smoke).
- Regression detection: store canonical experiment manifests in s3://redwood-fcs-sim/canon/ and run nightly compare job that flags >5% delta in any core metric.

Limitations and caveats
-----------------------
- Simulator is only as accurate as our kernel_latency_model. Hardware-level regressions (NVidia driver updates, new kernel patches) require re-benchmarking and updating the model.
- Fidelity mappings rely on historical A/Bs; changes to model families or prompt distributions require re-calibration.
- Synthetic traces may not capture long-tail adversarial user behavior; always complement with limited real-traffic canaries.

Planned enhancements (roadmap)
----------------------------
- 2027-Q2: integrate lightweight RL-based scenario exploration to suggest Pareto-optimal candidate rollouts.
- 2027-Q3: add per-route cost attribution to downstream product metrics (e.g., cost per conversion).
- 2027-Q4: connect simulator to canary automation to enable gated partial rollouts under supervised human review.

Appendix: simple example output (CSV excerpt)
---------------------------------------------

baseline,redwood-large-fp16,search-summarize,240,8.12,0.3,0.5
q8a-small-batch,redwood-large-q8a,search-summarize,265,6.98,1.9,3.2
q4_kv_warm,redwood-large-q4,search-summarize,252,6.48,2.4,1.1

Contact and escalation
----------------------
For questions or to request a custom simulation capacity-run, ping #bench-fcs-sim on Slack or email eng-bench@redwood.ai. For incidents where simulator output contradicts observed production metrics, open an incident and tag owners: @evelyn_chen, @ravi_malhotra, @marta_lopez.
